learningObjective: Create and set up backup policies (Standard and Enhanced), run backups on demand, and pick and run the right kind of restore.
engineer: Standard policy: one backup a day. Instant restore snapshots kept 1 to 5 days (default 2).

Enhanced policy: a backup every 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 hours. Instant restore snapshots kept 1 to 30 days (default 7). The portal requires it for Trusted Launch VMs, and it's needed for some disk types such as Premium SSD v2 and Ultra.
Retention: daily, weekly, monthly and yearly points. Daily points can be kept 7 to 9999 days.

How a VM backup works: the VM agent takes a snapshot. Where possible it's application-consistent (VSS on Windows, pre and post scripts on Linux). The snapshot is kept first as an instant restore snapshot, then copied to the vault.
Backup now: makes an extra recovery point straight away, with its own retention.

Restore options: Create new VM; Restore disks, to a staging storage account and resource group, then attach them or use the template Azure creates; Replace existing, which swaps the disks in place (the VM must still exist); Cross Region Restore, from a GRS vault with CRR turned on; File Recovery, which mounts a recovery point with a script so you can copy single files.
Azure Files backup: snapshot-based or vaulted, and restore a whole share or single files.
SQL Server in a VM: log backups every 15 minutes, so you can restore to a point in time.

example.title: Different policies for different VMs
body: Production SQL VMs (Trusted Launch) use an Enhanced policy: a backup every 4 hours, snapshots kept 7 days, and 30 daily, 12 monthly and 7 yearly points. A developer deletes a config file. In minutes, the admin gets it back with File Recovery from this morning's point.

architectureDecisions: Fast restores: keep instant restore snapshots long enough that most restores come from them.
Test restores: on a regular schedule, not only when something breaks.

misconceptions.myth: Backups survive a region outage by default.
misconceptions.reality: No. Only with a GRS vault and Cross Region Restore.

misconceptions.myth: File Recovery restores the whole VM.
misconceptions.reality: No. It mounts a recovery point so you can copy the files you need.

comparisons.difference: Copies VMs all the time for a fast failover (an RPO of minutes). Backup keeps older copies for a long time.
Copies you take by hand, with no policy and no vault retention.

troubleshooting.cause: The agent isn't running, or its outbound traffic is blocked.
troubleshooting.fix: Restart or update the agent, and allow the endpoints it needs.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't pick a Standard policy for a Trusted Launch VM.
troubleshooting.cause: The portal only offers Enhanced for Trusted Launch VMs.
troubleshooting.fix: Use an Enhanced policy (Standard only works through newer CLI, PowerShell or API versions).
Use Create new VM, or Restore disks.

configuration.limits: Standard policy: 1 backup a day, instant restore 1 to 5 days
Enhanced policy: every 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 hours, instant restore 1 to 30 days
configuration.permissions: Backup Contributor to manage vaults and policies (Monitoring Contributor for alerts and diagnostic settings)
